accepted.s: Who founded the Mitra Mela in 1899, which later became associated with Abhinav Bharat?
accepted.x: V.D. Savarkar founded Mitra Mela in 1899. It later developed into the revolutionary organisation Abhinav Bharat.
accepted.tq: Use the founder–organisation association without confusing Mitra Mela with other revolutionary bodies.
accepted.sec: Savarkar - societies, conspiracy case, imprisonment, books  [other exams]

accepted.s:
With reference to the Nasik Conspiracy Case, consider the following statements:
1. A.M.T. Jackson, the Nasik Collector, was assassinated by Anant Kanhere.
2. V.D. Savarkar was implicated in the case.
3. Savarkar was sentenced to imprisonment in the Cellular Jail at the Andamans.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The assassination of A.M.T. Jackson by Anant Kanhere led to Savarkar’s implication and sentence to life imprisonment in the Andamans.
accepted.tq: Check all three linked facts in a conspiracy-case cluster before selecting the combined option.
accepted.sec: Savarkar - societies, conspiracy case, imprisonment, books  [other exams]

accepted.s: V.D. Savarkar was arrested in London in 1910. At which place did his attempted escape fail?
accepted.x: Savarkar’s attempted escape failed at Marseilles in 1910.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the place of arrest and escape attempt from other overseas revolutionary centres.
accepted.sec: Savarkar - societies, conspiracy case, imprisonment, books  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Book — Year
1. The Indian War of Independence, 1857 — 1909
2. Hindutva — 1923
3. Mukti Kon Pathe — 1906
accepted.x: The first two pairs are correct for Savarkar’s books. Mukti Kon Pathe, published in 1906, was associated with Barindra Kumar Ghosh, not Savarkar.
accepted.tq: Separate authorship and dates carefully when books belong to the same revolutionary milieu.
accepted.sec: Savarkar - societies, conspiracy case, imprisonment, books  [other exams]

accepted.s: The police raid on the Maniktala bomb factory in 1908 was followed by the trial popularly known as the:
accepted.x: The raid on the Maniktala bomb factory in Calcutta led to the Alipore Bomb Case.
accepted.tq: Link the place of the police raid with the correctly named case.
accepted.sec: Alipore Bomb Case - accused, defence counsel, jail  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Alipore Bomb Case is NOT correct?
o: Barindra Ghosh was sentenced to life imprisonment in the Cellular Jail.
Narendranath Goswami was shot outside India by Madan Lal Dhingra.
Narendranath Goswami acted as an approver.
The accused were held in Alipore jail, Calcutta.
accepted.x: Narendranath Goswami was shot inside Alipore jail by Kanailal Dutta and Satyendranath Bose. He was not killed outside India by Madan Lal Dhingra.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped person and location in a case-related statement.
accepted.sec: Alipore Bomb Case - accused, defence counsel, jail  [other exams]

accepted.s: Who shot the approver Narendranath Goswami inside Alipore jail?
accepted.x: Kanailal Dutta and Satyendranath Bose shot Narendranath Goswami inside Alipore jail.
accepted.tq: Use the specific deed–revolutionary pair instead of a general case association.
accepted.sec: Alipore Bomb Case - accused, defence counsel, jail  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Chapekar brothers were associated with the assassination of:
accepted.x: Damodar and Balkrishna Chapekar shot Plague Commissioner W.C. Rand and Lt. Ayerst at Poona in 1897.
accepted.tq: Match the revolutionary action with the correct colonial officials.

accepted.s: The immediate background to the Chapekar brothers’ action at Poona in 1897 was:
accepted.x: The Chapekar brothers protested against the excesses of plague-control measures at Poona. The earlier revolutionary precedent mentioned in this context was Vasudev Balwant Phadke’s Ramosi force of 1879.
accepted.tq: Identify the cause behind an action rather than merely recalling its target.

accepted.s: At which railway station did Vanchi Aiyar shoot Robert Ashe, the Collector of Tirunelveli?
accepted.x: Vanchi Aiyar shot Robert Ashe at Maniyachi railway station on 17 June 1911 and then shot himself.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the location of a revolutionary action from locations of other cases.
accepted.sec: Revolutionaries in the South - Vanchi Aiyar

accepted.s:
Vanchi Aiyar was linked with which of the following associations or movements?
1. Bharata Matha Association
2. Swadeshi Steam Navigation agitation
3. V.O. Chidambaram Pillai

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Vanchi Aiyar was linked with the Bharata Matha Association and the Swadeshi Steam Navigation agitation associated with V.O. Chidambaram Pillai.
accepted.tq: Combine organisation, movement and leader associations from the same regional revolutionary context.
accepted.sec: Revolutionaries in the South - Vanchi Aiyar

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Bande Mataram — Aurobindo Ghosh
2. Ghadar di Goonj — Ghadar Party
3. The Philosophy of the Bomb — Bhagwati Charan Vohra
4. Why I am an Atheist — Bhagat Singh
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. These writings were associated respectively with Aurobindo Ghosh, the Ghadar Party, Bhagwati Charan Vohra and Bhagat Singh.
accepted.tq: Verify each author independently before choosing the comprehensive combination.
accepted.sec: Revolutionary writings and journals - author/editor  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Who was associated with the work Mukti Kon Pathe, published in 1906?
accepted.x: Mukti Kon Pathe, published in 1906, was associated with Barindra Kumar Ghosh.
accepted.tq: Test the less familiar author–work pair rather than the frequently repeated journal names.
accepted.sec: Revolutionary writings and journals - author/editor  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which of the following were Bengal journals associated with revolutionary activities?
1. Yugantar
2. Sandhya
3. Indian Sociologist

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Yugantar and Sandhya were Bengal journals associated with revolutionary activities. Indian Sociologist was associated with Shyamji Krishna Varma and the overseas revolutionary sphere.
accepted.tq: Use regional association to separate Bengal journals from overseas publications.
accepted.sec: Revolutionary writings and journals - author/editor  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which one of the following sets contains the birth dates correctly matched with the revolutionaries?
1. Bhagat Singh — 28 September 1907
2. Chandrashekhar Azad — 23 July 1906
3. Khudiram Bose — 3 December 1889
4. Ram Prasad Bismil — 11 June 1897
accepted.x: All four birth-date pairs are correct: Bhagat Singh, Chandrashekhar Azad, Khudiram Bose and Ram Prasad Bismil were born on the dates stated.
accepted.tq: Check each date–person pair instead of relying on a single familiar birth year.

accepted.s: After the death of Ram Prasad Bismil, Chandrashekhar Azad reorganised the Hindustan Republican Association as the:
accepted.x: Chandrashekhar Azad reorganised the Hindustan Republican Association into the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association after Bismil’s death.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the expansion and ideological change in a similarly named organisation.

accepted.s: Chandrashekhar Azad died at Alfred Park, Prayagraj, on:
accepted.x: Chandrashekhar Azad shot himself at Alfred Park, Prayagraj, on 27 February 1931.
accepted.tq: Separate a revolutionary’s birth date from the date and place of his final action.

accepted.s: Jatin Das died after how many days of hunger strike in Lahore jail in 1929?
accepted.x: Jatin Das died after 63 days of hunger strike in Lahore jail in 1929 and was regarded as the first martyr of that strike.
accepted.tq: Use the exact duration rather than confusing it with the date or place of the strike.

accepted.s:
Which of the following were associated with the founding of the Hindustan Republican Association?
1. Sachindranath Sanyal
2. Jogesh Chatterjee
3. Ram Prasad Bismil

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Sachindranath Sanyal, Jogesh Chatterjee and Ram Prasad Bismil were associated with the founding of the Hindustan Republican Association.
accepted.tq: Group the correct co-founders while avoiding substitution with later HSRA leaders.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Sukhdev — born at Ludhiana on 15 May 1907
Rajguru — born at Prayagraj on 27 February 1931
accepted.x: Sukhdev was born at Ludhiana on 15 May 1907. Rajguru was born in 1908 at Khed, now Rajgurunagar.
accepted.tq: Separate the birthplaces and dates of two closely associated revolutionaries.

accepted.s: Who among the following was associated with India House along with V.D. Savarkar and Lala Hardayal?
accepted.x: Madan Lal Dhingra was associated with India House along with Savarkar and Hardayal. Dhingra killed Curzon Wyllie in 1909.
accepted.tq: Identify the India House association without confusing it with the Berlin Committee or Kabul government.

accepted.s: Bhikaji Cama unfurled the Indian flag at Stuttgart in:
accepted.x: Bhikaji Cama unfurled the Indian flag at Stuttgart in 1907.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the year of the Stuttgart flag event from nearby revolutionary milestones.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Berlin Committee:
1. It was formed in 1915.
2. Virendranath Chattopadhyaya and Bhupendranath Dutta were associated with it.
3. It sought German and Turkish assistance for India’s freedom struggle.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Berlin Committee of 1915 included Virendranath Chattopadhyaya and Bhupendranath Dutta and sought German and Turkish help.
accepted.tq: Combine date, membership and objective in a foreign-centre revolutionary question.

accepted.s:
The Provisional Government of India established at Kabul in 1915 included:
1. Raja Mahendra Pratap
2. Barkatullah
3. Obaidullah Sindhi

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Raja Mahendra Pratap, Barkatullah and Obaidullah Sindhi were associated with the Provisional Government of India established at Kabul in 1915.
accepted.tq: Test the composition of the provisional government without substituting Berlin Committee members.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Formation of the Ghadar Party
B. Formation of the Hindustan Republican Association
C. Kakori action
D. Formation of the HSRA
accepted.x: The Ghadar Party was formed in 1913, the HRA in 1924, the Kakori action occurred in 1925 and the HSRA was formed in 1928.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place HRA before Kakori.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Muzaffarpur and Alipore cases
B. Killing of Curzon Wyllie
C. Bomb attack on Lord Hardinge
D. Ghadar revolt and Singapore Mutiny
accepted.x: The sequence is 1908 Muzaffarpur and Alipore cases, 1909 killing of Curzon Wyllie, 1912 Hardinge bomb and 1915 Ghadar revolt and Singapore Mutiny.
accepted.tq: Place the events by their stated milestone years and check the middle sequence.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Komagata Maru incident of 1914?
o: A ship carrying mainly Sikh passengers was refused entry into Canada and forced back to India.
A ship carried the Berlin Committee to Stuttgart for a political conference.
A ship carrying Indian troops mutinied at Singapore under Ghadar leadership.
A revolutionary vessel transported arms from Germany to Kabul.
accepted.x: The Komagata Maru carried 376 mainly Sikh passengers, who were refused entry into Canada and forced back to India.
accepted.tq: Identify the central event while separating it from the Singapore Mutiny and Berlin Committee.
accepted.sec: Komagata Maru and the Singapore Mutiny  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Komagata Maru incident:
1. The ship was forced back and reached Budge Budge.
2. Firing at Budge Budge killed 22 people.
3. The incident radicalised the Ghadar movement.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Budge Budge firing killed 22 people and contributed to the radicalisation of the Ghadar movement.
accepted.tq: Test the sequence, casualty figure and consequence of one incident together.
accepted.sec: Komagata Maru and the Singapore Mutiny  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Singapore Mutiny of February 1915 was led by Indian troops belonging to the:
accepted.x: The Singapore Mutiny involved Indian troops of the 5th Light Infantry and occurred under Ghadar influence.
accepted.tq: Match the mutiny with the correct military unit rather than a general Ghadar group.
accepted.sec: Komagata Maru and the Singapore Mutiny  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Ghadar revolt in Punjab in 1915 was fixed for:
accepted.x: The Ghadar revolt in Punjab was fixed for 21 February 1915, but the plan was betrayed and many participants were hanged under the Defence of India Act.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the planned date of revolt from dates of other revolutionary actions.
accepted.sec: Komagata Maru and the Singapore Mutiny  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Alluri Sitarama Raju was born in 1897 at:
accepted.x: Alluri Sitarama Raju was born in 1897 at Mogallu in West Godavari.
accepted.tq: Use the birthplace–leader association and eliminate locations belonging to other revolutionaries.

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about Alluri Sitarama Raju is correct?
1. He met Bengal revolutionaries at Chittagong in 1921.
2. He led the Rampa Rebellion from 1922 to 1924.
3. The rebellion opposed the Muttadari system and forest laws.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Raju’s contact with Bengal revolutionaries preceded his leadership of the Rampa Rebellion against the Muttadari system and forest laws.
accepted.tq: Combine biography, period and causes of a regional rebellion.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following places in the order of Alluri Sitarama Raju’s attacks:
A. Rajavommangi
B. Chintapalli
C. Krishnadevipeta
accepted.x: The sequence was Chintapalli, Krishnadevipeta and Rajavommangi.
accepted.tq: Start with the known first attack and preserve the sequence of the subsequent locations.

accepted.s: Who were the lieutenants associated with Alluri Sitarama Raju during the Rampa Rebellion?
o: Gam Mallu Dora and Gam Gantam Dora
accepted.x: Gam Mallu Dora and Gam Gantam Dora were associated with Alluri Sitarama Raju as lieutenants. Scott Coward and Haytes were officers killed during the rebellion.
accepted.tq: Separate revolutionary lieutenants from colonial officers mentioned in the same episode.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the Rampa Rebellion is NOT correct?
o: Scott Coward and Haytes were killed during the rebellion.
The Malabar Special Police was brought in against the rebels.
Alluri Sitarama Raju was killed on 7 May 1922.
A direct battle took place at Panjerighat.
accepted.x: Alluri Sitarama Raju was killed on 7 May 1924, not 1922. The other three statements are correct.
accepted.tq: Check the final date carefully when the rest of the statement contains true details.

accepted.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Tenali bomb case — Vande Mataram phase
2. Kakinada bomb case — Prativadi Bhayankaracharyulu
3. Darshi Chenchayya — Nenu Naa Desam

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All three pairs are correct. Prativadi Bhayankaracharyulu was sentenced to 14 years in the Andamans and wrote Andaman Jeevitam, while Darshi Chenchayya wrote Nenu Naa Desam on Ghadar.
accepted.tq: Verify each regional case–person–work association before selecting the complete combination.
